requirements.note: All 320 sorted by last name in inset-grouped letter sections. The section index (with a ★ entry) jumps on tap and scrubs on drag.
Filters live by name, company, formatted or digits-only phone, and email. Shows a 'No Results' state and '1 result' footer; clear and close restore the full list.
Detail shows avatar, name, company, phone, email and birthday (birthday row hidden when unknown). Phone and email are tinted rows with icons and an outward arrow.
Add/Remove from Favorites toggle on details, plus a Favorite badge. Favorites show at the top as a horizontal avatar carousel with a count; it updates at once.

Sheet form with labelled fields. Save is disabled for empty or whitespace-only names, and there is helper text. Return moves to the next field. Cancel on a dirty form asks to discard. Edit uses the same form, and re-sorting works (Aaronson→Young moved to Y).
Native swipe-to-delete in the list and a Delete Contact button on details, both with a confirmation alert; the count updates.
Deletes, the added and edited contact, and favorite changes all survived relaunch.

bugs: Once, right after closing search while the large title re-expanded, tapping a row only highlighted it (stayed selected) and did not open details; a second tap worked.
tells: Custom teal tint everywhere instead of the system accent, and colourful pastel initial avatars on every row; it looks styled rather than stock.
Favorites are a horizontal avatar carousel inside the list. The 5th avatar is cut off at the edge, and at the largest text size the avatar sits off-centre from its huge name label.
The nav bar is inconsistent: at launch it shows a small centred 'Contacts / 320 contacts' title, but after search it turns into a large title.
Rows are tall (84 pt), larger than system contact rows.
Section headers scroll away rather than sticking (inset-grouped style); acceptable, but unlike the Contacts app.
A.scroll: Smooth: no blank rows, pop-in or jumps during slow drags, flings or rubber-banding; the scroll-edge blur under the nav bar behaves natively. Index scrubbing jumps cleanly.

requirements.note: Plain list sorted by last name with sticky letter headers and a blue system-style section index that jumps on tap. The index has no entry for Favorites.

Bottom search bar (iOS 26 style) filters live by name, company, phone (formatted or digits) and email. Shows a '1 Contact' footer and a 'No Contacts Found' state with Clear Search; clearing restores the list.
Contacts-app-style card with initials, name, company, and blue phone/email values; the birthday row shows only when known.
Add/Remove from Favorites row on details. Favorites appear as a full section of rows at the top and update immediately.

Sheet with ✕/✓ buttons and placeholder-only fields. ✓ is disabled for empty or whitespace names, and names are trimmed. Edit uses the same form, and re-sorting works. Return dismisses the keyboard instead of moving to the next field, and closing a dirty form throws away changes without asking.
Native swipe-to-delete (no confirmation, as in iOS lists) and Delete Contact on details with a confirmation alert.
Deletes, the added and edited contact, and favorite toggles all survived relaunch.

bugs: Cancelling (✕) an edited form discards the edits silently, with no 'Discard Changes?' prompt.
tells: Each favorite row has a grey filled star that reads as disabled rather than as a favorite marker.
The Favorites section repeats 31 full rows before 'A', pushing the alphabetical list a screen and a half down, and the index has no ★ to jump back to it.
Return does not advance between fields in the form.
During the swipe-to-delete the row's subtitle (company) disappeared.
B.scroll: Very native: sticky section headers, scroll-edge blur, large title collapsing to inline, smooth flings with no blank rows or pop-in, and clean rubber-banding at the top.

why: Both meet every requirement and persist correctly. B is closer to the stock Contacts app: system blue, sticky plain list, bottom search, large title. A is more complete and careful in behaviour: it confirms before discarding edits and before swipe-deletes, Return moves between fields, there is a ★ index entry and labelled form fields, and a compact favorites strip that doesn't push the list down. A's custom teal styling and inconsistent title are the main costs, but I would rather ship A.
